scope: All 412 level2 units indexed and routed; 22 narrow source-to-lesson promotion proposals manually inspected. This is not exhaustive 412-unit semantic/visual acceptance.

proposals.reason: All seven standard-setting dimensions are explicitly taught: purpose, method, tools, order, scope, quality and standard time.
The purpose of the task is explicitly one of the teaching standards.
The tools to use are explicitly one of the teaching standards.
The target scope is explicitly one of the teaching standards.
Required finish quality is explicitly one of the teaching standards.
Standard completion time is explicitly one of the teaching standards.
Specific performance feedback, further practice, later follow-up and recorded skill gaps operationalize the narrow follow-up item.
Self-firefighting organization and explicit assignment and substitute roles.
Firefighting, reporting and evacuation drills with participants and follow-up records.
Supervision of fire sources and handling.
Occupant-capacity management is explicitly included in the management scope.
Fire-prevention education is explicitly included in the management scope.
Disaster reporting and evacuation guidance are assigned and practiced.
Liaison with fire authorities is explicitly included in the management scope.
The food sanitation inspector/manager qualification routes are explicitly named; this is the narrow route, not certification of the whole qualification regime.

Every profession in the source item is named: cook, confectionery hygienist, nutritionist, ship cook, slaughterhouse sanitation/work sanitation managers and poultry-processing sanitation manager. Current-source addition of registered dietitian is preserved.
Working under the business operator’s instructions is stated explicitly.
Animals are excluded from food-handling areas; animal-interaction customer seating does not authorize entry into kitchen/storage areas.
Regular thermometer accuracy checking plus date/method/result records and repair/replacement/follow-up cover this narrow calibration item.
Abnormal or disaster-suspect water use is stopped, affected products identified, testing and facility checks arranged, public-health consultation sought and restart evidence recorded.
One-year water test-certificate retention and extension to the longer food use/consumption period are explicitly taught.

The purpose of preparation is independently explained with washing, bitterness removal, scoring and rehydration; quality, preventing microbial multiplication and preventing contamination of finished food are all addressed.
